en: Parittattikādi (The Triplet of Limited States, etc.)
Dependent on a limited state, a limited state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root: twenty-two;
under object: eleven; under predominance: eighteen …pe… under mutuality: sixteen …pe… under prenascence and repetition: nine …pe… under non-disappearance: twenty-two.
Dependent on a state with limited object, a state with limited object arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to the root condition, there are thirteen; with respect to the object condition, thirteen; with respect to the predominance condition, nine … pe … with respect to the prenascence and repetition conditions, nine … pe … with respect to the non-disappearance condition, thirteen.
Dependent on a state that is not inferior, an intermediate state arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. With respect to the root condition, there are eighteen;
with respect to the object condition, nine … pe … with respect to the result condition, three … pe … with respect to the non-disappearance condition, eighteen.
Dependent on a state fixed in wrongness (*micchattaniyata*), a state fixed in rightness (*sammattaniyata*) arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).

(Abbreviated. Under the root condition there are eighteen; under the object condition (*ārammaṇa*) nine ... pe ... under the result condition (*vipāka*) three ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*) eighteen.
Dependent on a state not having the Path as its object (*namaggārammaṇa*), a state rooted in the Path (*maggahetuka*) arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition, there are twenty-six; ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance, there are twenty-six.
